title: GovernanceFinding
description: A single portfolio governance finding, persisted as one element of the array at snapshots/governance.json on the repo-butler-data orphan branch. Produced deterministically by src/governance.js (standards-gap, policy-drift, tier-uplift, tier-regression, open-vulnerability), src/dependabot-audit.js (dependabot-stale), src/butler-pr-audit.js (stale-butler-pr) and src/stalled-alert.js (stalled-alert). Every finding carries a `remediation` plan (ADR-007) — an executor routing hint plus a change spec — consumed by the MCP get_governance_findings tool, the dashboard, the repo-butler-apply skill, and any future hosted agent.

type.description: The finding category, which determines the remaining fields.

priority.description: Remediation priority. standards-gap derives it from adoption rate; tier-uplift and dependabot-stale from severity; policy-drift is always medium.

tool.description: standards-gap only: the standard/tool key (e.g. code-scanning, dependabot-actions, contributing-guide).

repo.description: policy-drift, tier-uplift, tier-regression, dependabot-stale, open-vulnerability, stale-butler-pr, stalled-alert: the affected repository name.

nonCompliant.description: standards-gap only: repos missing the standard.

sources.description: open-vulnerability only: which scanner(s) fired. Only `dependabot`-sourced findings are fixable by enabling Dependabot security updates; code-scanning/secret-scanning need a code change or secret rotation.

critical.description: open-vulnerability only: count of open critical Dependabot + code-scanning alerts.

high.description: open-vulnerability only: count of open high Dependabot + code-scanning alerts.

secretScanning.description: open-vulnerability only: count of open secret-scanning alerts.

max_severity.description: open-vulnerability only: peak urgency of the finding — `critical` when an open critical alert or any secret-scanning hit is present (secrets are treated as critical-urgency), else `high`.

autofixEnabled.description: open-vulnerability, dependabot-sourced only (ADR-012 Phase 3): whether GitHub's Dependabot automated security fixes are actively opening the bump PRs. true = remediation in flight (enabled and not paused); false = OFF/paused (not being driven to resolution); null = state unreadable/unknown. Read in the OBSERVE/portfolio-details layer (detection stays pure). When true and Dependabot is the only source, a high-priority finding is downgraded to medium; max_severity is never changed and the health-tier drop stands.

stalePRs.description: dependabot-stale and stale-butler-pr: the unmerged PRs behind the finding. stale-butler-pr entries additionally carry prClass/state/verified.

prClass.description: stale-butler-pr only: which butler workflow opened it. roadmap-update PRs are excluded from staleness — UPDATE rewrites their head every pipeline run, so their CI is permanently in flight and their age never resets.

state.description: stale-butler-pr only. Derived from the four-way prCiState (NOT prCiGreen, which collapses red/pending/no-CI/error into one false): awaiting-human = green and simply unmerged; blocked-persistent = the identical check set failed the last 3 attempts, so a rebase will not clear it; blocked-transient = red without that repeat evidence; ci-none = the repo has no CI at all, so nothing is blocking it; unknown = CI state unreadable, which never downgrades to an all-clear; unclassified = beyond the per-repo classification cap.

verified.description: stale-butler-pr only: whether the PR body carries a butler marker or the governance-apply label. A branch prefix is forgeable, so false means the branch claims to be the butler's but carries no corroboration — surfaced rather than dropped.

failing.description: stale-butler-pr only: names of the failing workflow runs on the most recent attempt.

alerts.description: stalled-alert only (G13): the open Dependabot alerts past the age threshold with no open Dependabot PR addressing them. A grouped Dependabot PR (whose branch names no package) in the same ecosystem and directory counts as possibly addressing an alert and suppresses it — the detector errs toward silence, because a false positive costs trust in every row.

number.description: The Dependabot alert number on the affected repo.

package.description: The vulnerable package name, as the alert reports it.

ecosystem.description: The alert's package ecosystem (npm, pip, actions, ...). Only npm alerts can be classified; every other ecosystem is reported with classification `unknown`.

manifestPath.description: The manifest the alert names. Its directory is what the classifier reads package.json and package-lock.json from, and what a grouped Dependabot branch is compared against.

severity.description: Advisory severity. The detector's floor is `medium`, deliberately below open-vulnerability's critical/high bar — the live case that motivated G13 was a medium alert open for 35 days, invisible to every other signal.

ageDays.description: Days the alert has been open.

classification.description: Why the alert is stuck, from src/trimmer.js planOverride called READ-ONLY (ADR-014). `reachable-by-update` means a lockfile refresh clears it and nobody has run one; `direct-dependency` means bump it normally; the rest need a human decision. `override` means a parent-scoped override WOULD clear it — reported as a classification and never acted on, since making that jump is ADR-013's business. `unknown` is the fail-closed value for an unreadable/unparseable manifest or lockfile, or an ecosystem with no classifier; the finding is still emitted, because the alert is stale whether or not we can explain it.

detail.description: The classifier's own one-line explanation, capped at 200 characters. Built from target-repo lockfile contents, so it is escaped on the dashboard and deliberately never enters the IDEATE prompt.

RemediationPlan.title: RemediationPlan
RemediationPlan.description: The portable remediation contract (ADR-007 Track B stage 1). Built deterministically by buildRemediationPlan() in src/governance.js — no LLM.

executor.description: Routing hint: `template` for findings the butler can write as a static file, `settings` for findings enabled via a repository-settings/ruleset write (ADR-009, e.g. code-review-bot), `agent` for findings needing tailored reasoning, `manual` for findings needing human judgement. A hint, not a guarantee the apply phase can act on it today.

targetFiles.description: Files the remediation would create or modify. Empty when the change is a repo-settings toggle or a human/legal decision rather than a file write.

intent.description: One-line statement of what the remediation does.

rationale.description: Why the finding fired, phrased deterministically from the finding's own fields.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conditions that, once true, mean the finding is resolved.
